source_refs.note: Exercise 3.4, Question 14: Exercise 3.4, book page 94: Q1-Q15 (integration by partial fractions); answers book pages 301-302

blocks.explanation:
Yeh trigonometric shakal mein chhupa hua rational function hai. Numerator mein \(\cos x\,dx\) hai, jo \(\sin x\) ka differential hai.
To \(t = \sin x\) rakhne se sawal \(\int \frac{dt}{t^3 - 1}\) ban jata hai.
\(t^3 - 1 = (t - 1)(t^2 + t + 1)\), aur \(t^2 + t + 1\) irreducible hai, yani Case-III.
Plan: substitution, partial fractions, quadratic wale hisse ka integral completing the square se, aur aakhir mein wapas \(\sin x\).
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\int \frac{\cos x}{\sin^3 x - 1}\,dx\).
Maloom karna: yeh integral.
Tareeqa: substitution \(t = \sin x\), phir partial fractions (Case-III). Pehchan ka tareeqa: jab integrand mein kisi function \(g(x)\) ke saath us ka derivative \(g'(x)\) bhi multiply ho raha ho, to \(t = g(x)\) rakhein.

\(t = \sin x\) rakhein
\[dt = \cos x\,dx\]
\[\int \dfrac{\cos x}{\sin^3 x - 1}\,dx = \int \dfrac{dt}{t^3 - 1}\]
Kyun: \(\sin x\) ka derivative \(\cos x\) hai, is liye \(\cos x\,dx\) poora ka poora \(dt\) ban gaya, aur neeche \(\sin^3 x = t^3\).

Factorise kar ke torein
\[t^3 - 1 = (t - 1)(t^2 + t + 1)\]
\[\dfrac{1}{(t - 1)(t^2 + t + 1)} = \dfrac{A}{t - 1} + \dfrac{Bt + C}{t^2 + t + 1}\]
\[1 = A(t^2 + t + 1) + (Bt + C)(t - 1) \quad (1)\]
Kyun: Cubes ka formula \(a^3 - b^3 = (a - b)(a^2 + ab + b^2)\), yahan \(a = t\), \(b = 1\). \(t^2 + t + 1\) ka discriminant \(b^2 - 4ac = 1 - 4 = -3\) negative hai, is liye yeh real linear factors mein nahi tootta: upar \(Bt + C\).

Constants nikalein
\[t = 1:\ 1 = 3A,\ A = \tfrac{1}{3}\]
\[t^2:\ 0 = A + B,\ B = -\tfrac{1}{3}\]
\[\text{constant}:\ 1 = A - C,\ C = -\tfrac{2}{3}\]
Kyun: \(t = 1\) par doosra term zero, aur \(1 + 1 + 1 = 3\). Left side sirf 1 hai, is mein \(t^2\) ka coefficient 0 aur constant 1. Right side ka \(t^2\) coefficient \(A + B\) aur constant \(A - C\).

Nayi shakal
\[\dfrac{1}{t^3 - 1} = \dfrac{1}{3}\cdot\dfrac{1}{t - 1} - \dfrac{1}{3}\cdot\dfrac{t + 2}{t^2 + t + 1}\]
\[t + 2 = \dfrac{1}{2}(2t + 1) + \dfrac{3}{2}\]
Kyun: \(Bt + C = -\frac{1}{3}(t + 2)\). Quadratic wale fraction ka integral karne ka tareeqa: numerator mein denominator ka derivative \(2t + 1\) banao. \(\frac{1}{2}(2t + 1) = t + \frac{1}{2}\), aur \(t + 2\) tak pohanchne ke liye \(\frac{3}{2}\) aur chahiye.

Quadratic wale hisse ka integral
\[\int \dfrac{t + 2}{t^2 + t + 1}\,dt\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{2}\ln(t^2 + t + 1) + \dfrac{3}{2}\int \dfrac{dt}{\left(t + \frac{1}{2}\right)^2 + \frac{3}{4}}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{2}\ln(t^2 + t + 1) + \sqrt{3}\tan^{-1}\dfrac{2t + 1}{\sqrt{3}}\]
Kyun: Pehla hissa \(\frac{f'}{f}\) shakal ka hai, to \(\ln\). Doosre mein completing the square: \(t^2 + t + 1 = (t + \frac{1}{2})^2 + \frac{3}{4}\), yani \(a^2 = \frac{3}{4}\), \(a = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\). Formula \(\frac{1}{a}\tan^{-1}\frac{u}{a}\) se \(\frac{3}{2}\cdot\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}} = \sqrt{3}\) aur \(\frac{t + 1/2}{\sqrt{3}/2} = \frac{2t + 1}{\sqrt{3}}\).
Dhyan dein: \(\frac{3}{\sqrt{3}} = \sqrt{3}\) hota hai, 1 nahi.

Jor kar wapas \(x\) mein
\[\dfrac{1}{3}\ln|t - 1| - \dfrac{1}{6}\ln(t^2 + t + 1)\]
\[- \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\tan^{-1}\dfrac{2t + 1}{\sqrt{3}} + c\]
Kyun: Quadratic wala poora hissa \(-\frac{1}{3}\) se multiply hua: \(-\frac{1}{3}\cdot\frac{1}{2} = -\frac{1}{6}\) aur \(-\frac{1}{3}\sqrt{3} = -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\). Phir \(t = \sin x\) rakha. \(t^2 + t + 1\) hamesha positive hai, is liye us par modulus nahi chahiye; \(t - 1 = \sin x - 1\) zero ya negative hota hai, is liye wahan modulus zaroori hai.

Tasdeeq (constants)
\[\tfrac{1}{3}(t^2 + t + 1) - \tfrac{1}{3}(t + 2)(t - 1)\]
\[= \tfrac{1}{3}(t^2 + t + 1 - t^2 - t + 2)\]
\[= 1 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: \((t + 2)(t - 1) = t^2 + t - 2\). Partial fractions ko wapas jora to numerator 1 aaya, yani \(\frac{1}{t^3 - 1}\) wapas mil gaya.

blocks.text: Kitab ke aakhir mein answers (page 302) mein Exercise 3.4 ke jawab ghalat heading "Exercise 3.6" ke neeche chhape hain. Is sawal ka jawab us block ka item (xiv) hai: \(\frac{1}{3}\ln|\sin x - 1| - \frac{1}{6}\ln(\sin^2 x + \sin x + 1) - \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{2\sin x + 1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) + c\). Yeh jawab sahi hai. Jis block par "Exercise 3.4" likha hai (page 301) woh kisi aur exercise ke jawab hain, is liye wahan se milane ki koshish na karein.
